accessibility_requirement_results.basis: Lead runtime locale switch retained event identity; reducer preserves pattern/event; bilingual runtime copy and registry text are selected by locale.
Source review: native labelled select/input, fieldset legend, named buttons, labelled panels and feedback status in both locales.
Native controls plus Lead keyboard/accessibility-tree Next and Previous; all remaining actions use the same native button/input/select semantics.
Scoped 3px focus-visible outline with 3px offset exists for button/input/select and no ancestor clips it.
Native disabled boundaries are coded for Previous, Next, Play, Pause and observed during browser transport testing.
Pre-existing polite atomic runtime announcer and separate polite input revision region are present; event action text changes from shared state.
Reduced-motion media rule removes transition/animation duration while reducer event order and one-step checkpoint behavior are unchanged.
Current trace uses aria-current plus Current text and border; completed steps use a check mark; feedback uses check/exclamation and text; sync uses repeated identity text.
Every required panel is a labelled article/section/status surface with a visible or screen-reader heading.
Lead runtime measurement at 320 by 800: scrollWidth 305 <= viewport width 320; production console errors empty.
Source DOM order places code/state/trace/output/invariant, prediction/feedback and then controls; narrow layout is one column.
Responsive grids collapse at 64rem/42rem and the stricter 320 CSS-pixel runtime test has no horizontal page overflow. Dedicated browser 200 percent zoom remains an S8-D spotcheck.
Noscript fallback includes bilingual heading, code locator, before/change/after and invariant; it explicitly states that interactivity needs JavaScript.
All five panels read one event object and Lead exercised deterministic event changes; code/state expose the same data-sync-event.
Reducer pauses after one PLAY step and Lead observed one-step pause; prediction appears before manually advancing again.
Lead submitted prediction; source feedback names correctness/expected event, includes event feedback, uses text/symbol and does not change event index.
Bilingual memory cue names the current event and gives the reusable event-predict-invariant-output action sequence.
Lead observed change-input revision; reducer resets event/prediction/play and increments the exposed revision shared by the current runtime.

pedagogy_check_results.basis: Route gives Paper 4 scope/practice instructions; root heading, pattern selector and progress expose orientation.
Lead observed Play advance one step and pause; learner must predict before another advance.
Prediction prompt is sourced from the current Stage 7 event and input expects the next event name/type.
Runtime prediction test plus source feedback: correctness, expected event, event explanation and continuation action are present.
One current event drives code/state/trace/output/invariant; deterministic browser transport and data-sync-event confirm the join.
State panel and fallback visibly label Before, Change and After, with structural sections independent of colour.
Invariant panel is derived from the current event and remains adjacent to trace/output in the learning grid.
Memory cue gives a stable four-action solve/check routine in meaning-equivalent VI/EN and prefixes the current event.
Lead exercised Next/Previous, Play one-step pause, Reset, STACK_PUSH selection and change-input revision; all state transitions are deterministic.
Semantic panels keep the current change and actions distinct; 320 px runtime remains within the viewport without page overflow.
Locale runtime test preserves event identity; source selects purpose, prompts, feedback, invariant and memory routine by locale.
Final-event completion, reset, memory routine and observed change-input revision support immediate transfer to a new run.

limitations_carried_to_s8_d: A8 should run one named screen-reader/AX announcement spotcheck for Next, Reset and change-input; S8-C verified semantics and Lead accessibility-tree operation.
A8 should explicitly emulate prefers-reduced-motion and compare event IDs; S8-C verified the media rule and deterministic reducer path.
A8 should perform a dedicated 200 percent browser zoom spotcheck; S8-C has source reflow evidence and a stricter 320 CSS-pixel no-overflow runtime measurement.

gate_decision.rationale: All seven resubmitted required findings are independently closed against source and Lead runtime evidence. All 18 accessibility requirements and 12 pedagogy checks have sufficient S8-C evidence; three explicit environment spotchecks remain assigned to final S8-D QA without reopening an implementation finding.
